image_spec.headline: Pick Friday's leftover dinner now, before the feast.
image_spec.body: Save turkey soup or sandwiches to Friday, Nov 27. On the Family plan, everyone at home sees it.
image_spec.tip: Thursday is the feast. Friday is covered.

posts.caption:
Every year it goes the same way. Thursday is great, then Friday shows up with a mountain of turkey in the fridge and nobody has a plan.

So we're picking Friday's dinner now. Turkey noodle soup at our house, and sandwiches with the last of the cranberry sauce for lunch.

In StashSmart you can save a recipe to a date in Meals, so on Friday it's just there. On the Family plan the whole house can see it, which means fewer "what's for dinner?" texts. 🍗

Soup or sandwiches? One word is fine. Coming soon on iPhone.

image_spec.headline: A 16 to 20 pound turkey needs 4 to 5 days to thaw in the fridge.
image_spec.body: Cooking Thursday? It moves from the freezer to the fridge on Saturday.
image_spec.tip: About 1 day for every 4 to 5 pounds.

posts.caption:
Quick math before the weekend. A 16 to 20 pound turkey needs 4 to 5 days to thaw in the fridge, according to the USDA. That's about one day for every 4 to 5 pounds.

So if you're cooking Thursday, the bird moves from the freezer to the fridge on Saturday. Set it on a tray on the bottom shelf so nothing drips. Once it's thawed, it's fine in there for another day or two.

Nobody wants to be running cold water over a frozen turkey at 6am on Thanksgiving. 🧊

Set a reminder for Saturday, then tag whoever's cooking this year.

posts.source_note: USDA FSIS, Let's Talk Turkey / The Big Thaw: thaw in the refrigerator about 24 hours per 4 to 5 pounds; 16 to 20 lb takes 4 to 5 days; a thawed turkey keeps 1 to 2 days in the refrigerator. https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/poultry/lets-talk-turkey-consumer-guide-safely-roasting
